title: KV grooming and serving-hint pipeline for paged attention
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Goal: Reduce tail latency and token cost variability introduced by paged attention when KV cache becomes fragmented, while enabling the serving runtime to select kernel variants and decode pacing based on lightweight request hints.

Motivation: We observe intermittent 95th-percentile latencies on long-context workloads when KV pages are fragmented across slabs and when prefill/decode scheduling unintentionally causes interleaved IO and kernel stalls. Existing eviction heuristics reclaim capacity but do not prioritize reuse-friendly layouts; kernels are chosen conservatively because the runtime lacks quick signals about expected sequence-length distribution and reuse locality.

Proposal summary:
1) KV grooming daemon (kv-groomer): a low-priority background task that compacts lightly fragmented page sets during low-util windows and builds short-lived relocation maps. It uses occupancy histograms and a fragmentation score to choose candidate pages for in-place consolidation or migration to hot slabs. Grooming operates within configured soft-reserve budgets per-tenant to avoid interfering with serving SLOs.
2) Fragmentation scoring: per-shard bloom-backed slot summaries + occupancy percentiles to estimate reclaim cost vs reuse benefit. Score components include live-usage-frequency, contiguous-run-length, and decode-affinity (prefill hit rate).
3) Slab-aware allocator: introduce a lightweight ring free-list per-slab that prefers allocations that preserve locality of recent KV lookups and reduces cross-slab accesses for typical 2–8k token prefills.
4) Deferred-eviction with confirmation: when eviction candidates are selected, mark slots as "pending-evict" for a short epoch (milliseconds) to allow in-flight decodes to finish or to accept cheap reuse (avoid thrashing).
5) Serving hints and kernel hinting: requests may carry short-form hints (sequence_length_est, expected_prefix_id, reuse_intent) computed at SDK/edge. The runtime consumes these hints to select kernel configurations (fast small-seq kernel vs batched large-seq kernel), prefetch thresholds, and whether to attempt KV pinning. Hints are optional and default to conservative selection.
6) Prefill/decode scheduler improvements: introduce decode waves with pacing gates to avoid IO + kernel overlap spikes. The scheduler uses a per-GPU in-flight token budget and admits prefill work based on predicted KV locality to reduce cross-shard IO contention.

Trade-offs considered:
- Background grooming improves reuse density and tail latency but consumes cycles and memory bandwidth. We limit grooming to off-peak windows and make budgets tunable per-customer.
- Adding request hints increases SDK complexity but gives large wins on GC-heavy multitenant workloads. We keep hints optional and additive.
- Deferred-eviction reduces thrash but can temporarily decrease available capacity; we bound epoch and reclaim aggressively under pressure.

Design artifacts and experiments:
- Design doc: confluence link in attachments.
- Microbenchmarks: local simulation shows 22% reduction in 95th latency for multi-tenant long-context chat workload with moderate grooming enabled (see Drive folder).
- PR: runtime changes are in github PR #1427 (allocator, grooming daemon, scheduler).

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase A (spike): instrumentation and offline sim (done) — scripts to compute fragmentation score from trace logs and simulate grooming moves.
- Phase B (impl): slab ring free-list + bloom-backed summaries + grooming daemon + deferred-evict (current work).
- Phase C (integration): serve hint ingestion + kernel routing hook + decode wave pacing.
- Phase D (canary & rollout): staged canary on dedicated pools, monitor tail latency, token-cost delta, and eviction churn.

Acceptance criteria / definition of done:
- KV grooming daemon can be toggled per-pool and respects soft-reserve budgets.
- Fragmentation score reduces measured slot fragmentation by >= 35% under test traces.
- 95th-percentile decode latency reduced by >= 15% for target workloads in canary runs without increasing average CPU/GPU utilization by more than 8%.
- No regression in single-tenant latency SLOs (median and p50 within 2% of baseline).
- Logging/metrics: grooming_moves, fragmentation_score, pending_evictions, kernel_hint_match_rate, decode_wave_backpressure are emitted and visible on the runtime dashboard.
- PR merged and rollout plan documented in the release notes.

Rollout / monitoring plan:
- Manual canary on dedicated pools (5% traffic) for 72h, compare dashboards and alert on: increase in eviction churn > 10x, grooming-induced GPU bandwidth > 6% sustained, or 95th latency regression > 5%.
- Gradual traffic ramp to 25% then 100% over 2 weeks if no alarms.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Better heuristics for multi-model diners where interleaving prefix IDs causes reuse patterns to be less stable. Consider adding short-lived prefix clustering keys in request hints.
- Explore kernel micro-benchmarks to verify that hint-driven kernel selection does not accidentally increase per-token micro-costs for certain models (planned lab measurements).
